clue.text: Give a warning to the left prior to conclusion

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship, as seen facing forward
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: Someone cautions others to keep left before something finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' looks like a direction for the warning but is a nautical synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or signal a coming event, often an unwelcome one, which serves as a warning.

clue.text: Comedy writer in children's area

parts.note: a comedy is a kind of play
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A comic author is found among the toddlers.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a small enclosure where a baby or toddler can play safely.

clue.text: Return to take exam again around six

indicators.note: around means the letters for take exam again go round the six

parts.note: to resit is to sit an exam a second time
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A student goes back to retake a test at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Resit is the British term for retaking an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit a place or topic is to go back to it.

clue.text: A world full of energy, skill and heart

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A planet brimming with vigour, talent and compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' is a link here; H for hearts comes from card notation, as in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is one world among others.

clue.text: Shift drink, and get rebuke

parts.note: a shift is a simple straight dress
to down a drink is to swallow it in one go

explanation.surface: After a work shift, someone has a drink and gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period but is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is an idiom for scolding them severely.

clue.text: Creeps call into church before Sunday

indicators.note: before means the first group comes ahead of the letter for Sunday
into means the call is placed inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a phone call into church ahead of the Sunday service.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs: one who cringes shrinks or cowers away, much as one who creeps behaves in a servile, fawning way.

clue.text: Trees manage to conceal skinhead

indicators.note: to conceal means the word for manage hides the next letter within it

parts.note: to cope is to manage
the head of the word skin is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide a shaven-headed youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a youth but means the first letter of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket or group of trees.

clue.text: Awful trait — gene pool mix!

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of trait and gene are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful characteristic gets blended into the population's genes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' only bolsters the picture of a gene pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate things is to combine or blend them into a whole.

clue.text: Shot a boss, given permission!

parts.note: a go is a shot or attempt
a head is a boss or chief

explanation.surface: Someone shoots their boss after being given clearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The go-ahead is approval or authorisation to start something.

clue.text: Unhappy about player, but honoured

indicators.note: about means the word for unhappy goes round the instrument

parts.note: sad means unhappy
a lute is a musical instrument, something that is played

explanation.surface: A sad musician is nonetheless paid tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' here is an instrument that plays music rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to pay tribute to them or acknowledge them with respect.

clue.text: Unfavourable notice on poet's output

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a poet produces verse

explanation.surface: A critic gives a poor review of a poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' suggests a review here, but it is a printed advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions or reviews are hostile or harmful, the opposite of favourable.

clue.text: Danger of drop after point is taken back

indicators.note: after means the drop comes later in the word than the point
taken back means the word for a point is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tip is the pointed end of something
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: Someone warns of a sheer drop once a promontory has been passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken back' turns TIP into PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden hazard or trap waiting to catch the unwary.

clue.text: Heat spots develop quickly

indicators.note: develop suggests the letters of heat spots changing into a new form

explanation.surface: In hot weather a rash of spots breaks out fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb for with great speed, from the haste of postal riders.

clue.text: Visitor putting energy into blow

indicators.note: putting into means the energy letter goes inside the word for a blow

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A visitor arrives with a burst of vigour, like a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone invited to stay or dine, that is, a caller or visitor.

clue.text: Cash paid for music?

definitions.meaning: musical sounds are written and played as a series of pitched tones

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether money was handed over for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper money and the written symbols of a tune share one plural word.

clue.text: That seals it — a lot sleep around!

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of a lot sleep being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping around a great deal is decisive proof of something.
explanation.walkthrough: SELLOTAPE is a British brand name for clear adhesive tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky tape is used to fasten parcels shut, so it closes up a package.

clue.text: Given to being on holiday with no thought for others

parts.note: someone off work is away on holiday
handed means given over

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker is accused of selfish, inconsiderate behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to being' just joins the pieces: HANDED is attached to OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhanded behaviour is casual and curt, showing little care or courtesy towards other people.

clue.text: Bodies flying?

parts.note: read as bodies hurled through the air, but meant as the main hulls of aircraft in flight

explanation.definitionFit: The main body section of an aeroplane, holding crew and passengers, has its own name.

clue.text: Marijuana factories and the growth in containers

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
industrial plants are factories

explanation.surface: Cannabis farms are set beside innocent greenery grown in tubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces first, then a straight definition of plants grown in pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot plants are houseplants cultivated in pots, so greenery raised in containers.

clue.text: Deaf cop displaying no humour

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective meaning humourless

indicators.note: displaying suggests the letters of deaf cop being laid out afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A police officer who cannot hear never laughs at jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is an adjective, here standing for having no humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A po-faced person has a solemn, disapproving expression lacking any sense of fun.

clue.text: Powerful relation

definitions.meaning: forceful and effective, as with a blow or argument
the narrating of a story, as one relates events

explanation.definitionFit: A forceful argument is a striking one, and recounting a tale is narrating it.

clue.text: Seam bowling caught ten in tests

indicators.note: caught means the scrambled letters hold the ten inside them
bowling suggests the letters of seam being sent spinning into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: In a cricket match, swing bowling takes ten catches during the Test series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowling' rearranges SEAM into EAMS, and 'caught' puts X inside it. Seam bowling is a cricket style using the ball's stitching; Tests are international cricket matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal tests of knowledge, as at school or university.

clue.text: The language of Ghana, if translated

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters of Ghana and if being converted into another form

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a West African country's speech would be rendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' fits the language surface but signals the letters rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghani is a term used for the speech of Afghanistan, commonly Pashto.

clue.text: Looking to understand piece

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to make sense of a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking means searching or trying to find, as does looking for something.

clue.text: Papers from government department backing fuel

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department

indicators.note: backing means the word for fuel runs in reverse

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Documents emerge from a ministry that supports energy supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OIL into LIO; 'backing' reads as support on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet or leaf of paper, or a set of loose documents in a folder.

clue.text: Fellow worker in firm left association

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a league is an association or alliance

explanation.surface: A co-worker at a company has joined a left-wing alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is someone you work alongside in the same job or profession.

clue.text: Thinks about cold chops

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to hew is to chop

explanation.surface: Someone ponders cold lamb chops.
explanation.walkthrough: To chew something over is to think about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing something over is mulling or pondering it at length.

clue.text: Draw out end, but crew regularly missing

indicators.note: regularly missing means every other letter of end but crew is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A crew finally gets pulled out, but some keep failing to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to elicit or bring out something latent.

clue.text: Accountant in china developing the bends

indicators.note: in means the accountant's letters sit inside the reworked word
developing signals the letters of the following word changing shape

parts.note: the setter's fodder, which as the anagram works must supply the letters of niche
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant posted to China is developing decompression sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'china' cannot supply the E; the anagram needs NICHE, reworked by 'developing' into CHI_NE around CA. 'the bends' poses as the diver's illness but means a series of road bends.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicane is a tight S-shaped sequence of turns placed on a racing circuit or road to slow traffic.

clue.text: Travel to old city with French friend — for fish!

parts.note: to go is to travel
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A tourist visits an ancient site with a Parisian pal to see some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gourami is a freshwater fish from Asia, popular in home aquariums.

clue.text: Pointed looks that can hurt?

parts.note: read one way these are hostile glares, as in the idiom about looking at someone with venom; read literally, they are sharp blades that wound

explanation.definitionFit: To look daggers is to glare with hostility, and the weapons themselves are short pointed knives that injure.

clue.text: Apparent visit to lib Dem leader

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
Sir Menzies 'Ming' Campbell led the Liberal Democrats in 2006-07

explanation.surface: A call is paid on the head of a British political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British party; their leader when this was set was Menzies Campbell, nicknamed Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming as an adjective means outwardly so, appearing true on the surface.
